aloe_vera.common_growing_areas: Tropical and subtropical regions worldwide; cultivated in Asia, Africa, Americas
aloe_vera.medicinal_properties: Topical soothing for burns and wounds; used in cosmetics; gel may have anti-inflammatory and moisturizing properties
aloe_vera.toxic_properties: Aloe latex (yellow sap) contains anthraquinones that can cause digestive upset if ingested in large amounts; topical use is generally safe for most people

aloevera.common_growing_areas: Similar to Aloe Vera: tropical and subtropical regions
aloevera.medicinal_properties: Soothing, moisturizing; used in topical preparations
aloevera.toxic_properties: Internal use of aloe latex may cause cramps and diarrhea

aloeveraa.toxic_properties: Not intended for internal consumption; may cause digestive upset

curry.common_growing_areas: Native to Indian subcontinent; grown in South and Southeast Asia
curry.medicinal_properties: Traditionally used as a digestive aid and antioxidant; leaves are used in culinary preparations and folk remedies
curry.toxic_properties: Generally regarded as safe when used as food; medicinal dosing should follow professional guidance

curry_leaves.medicinal_properties: Used in cooking and traditional medicine for digestion and blood sugar support
curry_leaves.toxic_properties: Safe as food; high-dose extracts should be used cautiously

hibiscus.medicinal_properties: Used in traditional medicine for mild diuretic effects, antioxidant properties, and hair care preparations
hibiscus.toxic_properties: Generally safe in culinary amounts; concentrated extracts should be used with care

neem.common_growing_areas: Indian subcontinent, parts of Africa and tropical regions
neem.medicinal_properties: Used traditionally for antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and skin-care applications; many topical formulations use neem extracts
neem.toxic_properties: Neem oil and high-dose internal use can be toxic, particularly to infants and in very large doses; follow professional guidance
